title: QUIZ - 33
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a radical by factoring out the largest perfect-square factor
questions.question: Simplify the radical expression: \( \sqrt{180} \)
questions.explanation: \(180 = 36 \times 5\), and 36 is a perfect square, so \( \sqrt{180} \) \(= 6\sqrt{5}\).
questions.hint: Factor out the largest perfect square from under the radical.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a radical by factoring out the largest perfect-square factor
questions.question: Simplify the radical expression: \( \sqrt{108} \)
questions.explanation: \(108 = 36 \times 3\), and 36 is a perfect square, so \( \sqrt{108} \) \(= 6\sqrt{3}\).
questions.hint: Factor out the largest perfect square from under the radical.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate the square root of a perfect square
questions.question: Evaluate: \( \sqrt{121} \)
questions.hint: Find the number that, when multiplied by itself, gives the value under the radical.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a radical by factoring out the largest perfect-square factor
questions.question: Simplify the radical expression: \( \sqrt{24} \)
questions.explanation: \(24 = 4 \times 6\), and 4 is a perfect square, so \( \sqrt{24} \) \(= 2\sqrt{6}\).
questions.hint: Factor out the largest perfect square from under the radical.

questions.learningObjective: Estimate the value of a square root that is not a perfect square by bounding it between integers
questions.question: Between which two consecutive whole numbers does \( \sqrt{88} \) lie?
questions.hint: Find the perfect squares just below and just above the given number.
